executive_assessment.text: The NDC describes GLOF risk in the upper Indus; storms and seawater intrusion on the Balochistan and Sindh coasts; river floods and agricultural heat in Punjab and Sindh; and aridity across parts of Punjab, Sindh, and Balochistan.
The NDC reports Pakistan contributes about 0.9% of global GHG emissions yet is highly climate-vulnerable, citing floods, rainfall shifts, glacier melt, and vector-borne disease.

geographic_notes.text: upper Indus Basin; Balochistan coast; Sindh coast; Punjab; Sindh; Balochistan: The NDC describes GLOF risk in the upper Indus; storms and seawater intrusion on the Balochistan and Sindh coasts; river floods and agricultural heat in Punjab and Sindh; and aridity across parts of Punjab, Sindh, and Balochistan.
Pakistan; 94 calamity-hit districts: The PDNA reports 2022 floods affected 33 million people, displaced nearly 8 million, and killed over 1,700; 94 districts were calamity-hit by October 11.
Sindh; 94 calamity-hit districts: The PDNA estimates 780,000 houses destroyed and 1.27 million partly damaged; Sindh accounted for 83% of housing damage.

known_gaps.text: The 2021 NDC is a dated national synthesis; updated province-level climate and food-security indicators were not checked.
The PDNA is a rapid post-disaster assessment based on data collected September to mid-October 2022; it warns that inaccessible areas and time constraints limit accuracy.
The PDNA reports flood impacts but does not establish climate-change attribution for the 2022 event.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
